panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Makeup Set = Fund / ETF
A fund is like a pre-made makeup set.
Instead of picking each stock yourself, you
buy one package with a mix inside.
Professionals build it for you.
Examples:
All-skincare set = tech fund
Mixed everyday glam kit = index fund
Fund = A bundle of stocks in one purchase
panels.scene: Living room with text overlay explaining funds as makeup sets.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Let's talk about the stock market - explained with makeup✨

☑️ The Stock Market= Sephora
Imagine the stock market is like Sephora.
It's a giant store where you can shop from different brands.
In investing, you're choosing between different companies.

💅 Each Brand = A Company
Each makeup brand represents a company.
In the stock market, companies offer stocks—
which you can buy.

💄 One Product = One Stock
A stock is like one product.
If you buy Rare Beauty blush, that's like buying one stock
in Rare Beauty.
You now own a small piece of the company.
panels.scene: Woman taking mirror selfie in beauty salon explaining stock market with makeup analogy.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Stock Value = Product Hype
When a product goes viral —like Dior Lip Oil— its value goes up because demand is high.

Same with stocks. If a company grows and performs well, the price of its stock usually increases.

If people lose interest or the company underperforms, the stock price can drop.

💄 Makeup Bag = Diversified Portfolio
If you only invest in one stock, it's risky.
But if you build a mix—just like a good makeup bag—you're more prepared

If your whole bag was just lipsticks, you'd struggle.
But when you have a full set, you're ready for anything.
That's diversification—owning different types of stocks and funds to stay safe.
panels.scene: Gold shelves display beauty products with text overlays explaining stock market concepts using makeup bag analogy.

Retatrutide (Reta)
Triple hormone activator. Lowers hunger hard
and increases energy burn. Stronger than
semaglutide for fat loss.
Dose used in studies: 2-12 mg weekly
(titrated slowly).
Fat loss often visible in 4-8 weeks.
Side effects: nausea, vomiting, low appetite,
fatigue. Still in clinical trials.
panels.scene: Black background text panel about Retatrutide weight loss drug

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
Tesamorelin
Strong growth hormone releaser. Often used
to reduce deep belly fat.
Typical dose: 2 mg daily, often at night.
Visible belly fat changes in 4-8 weeks.
Can cause water retention and joint tightness.
panels.scene: Text-only panel describing Tesamorelin for belly fat reduction

panels.subject: face_skin
panels.ocrText:
GHK-Cu
Improves skin quality and healing. Boosts
collagen for firmer skin.
Typical dose: 1-2 mg daily (injection or topical
use).
Skin changes usually seen in 4-8 weeks.
Rare skin irritation if topical.
panels.scene: Text-only panel detailing GHK-Cu skincare benefits and usage.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4)
Helps repair tissue and improve blood flow to
injured areas. Used for bigger injuries.
Typical dose: 2-5 mg per week, split into 2
shots, for 4-6 weeks.
Results usually show in 2-4 weeks.
Possible fatigue or mild headache.
panels.scene: Black background text panel about TB-500

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
BPC-157
Speeds up healing in tendons, ligaments,
 muscle, and gut lining. Popular for stubborn
 injuries.
 Typical dose: 250-500 mcg daily (split
 morning and night).
 Most notice less pain in 1-3 weeks.
 Side effects are rare, sometimes mild nausea
 or headache.
panels.scene: Black background text panel about BPC-157 healing properties

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
CJC-1295 (no DAC) + Ipamorelin
Signals your body to release more growth
hormone. Helps with muscle growth, fat loss,
recovery, and sleep.
Typical dose: 100–200 mcg of each, 1–3 times
daily. Often before bed.
Sleep improves in 1–2 weeks. Body changes in
6–12 weeks.
Possible water retention, tingling hands, mild
hunger.
panels.scene: Text panel detailing CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin stack benefits

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
IGF-1 LR3
Insulin-like Growth Factor. Directly tells
muscle cells to grow. Much stronger than GH
alone.
Common dose: 20-50 mcg daily (short cycles
4-6 weeks).
Muscle fullness felt in 1-2 weeks.
Risks: low blood sugar, organ growth if
abused.

If you are considering taking GLP-1s to manage PCOS, I highly highly highly recommend working with a dietitian.

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
Why are we considering taking GLP-1s with PCOS?
Many individuals with PCOS have elevated insulin levels.
About 70% of women with PCOS have some degree of insulin resistance.
Signs of insulin resistance:
•abdominal weight gain
•skin tags
•increased hunger
•sweet cravings
•dark patches behind the neck / groin area
High insulin levels can cause more imbalanced hormone levels.
This is why GLP-1s may help women with PCOS.
panels.scene: Healthy salad on plate with city view background

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
First, what are GLP-1s?
Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro are all types/brands of GLP-1 medications.
These drugs mimic a hormone called glucagon-like peptide 1, which lowers blood sugar levels.
This is why GLP-1s have been prescribed to folks with type 2 diabetes for 10+ years.
We have found over the years that these medications can cause secondary weight loss in some individuals.
panels.scene: Urban street scene with buildings and text overlay

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
How do GLP-1s help lower blood sugar?
They delay stomach emptying & food gets digested slower, which helps stabilize blood sugars.
It can increase insulin production to help lower blood sugar post meal.
Reduces sugar that gets released from the liver.
panels.scene: Snowy forest with text overlay about GLP-1s

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
Do I believe in GLP-1s for PCOS?

I believe in body autonomy. I believe that you should make an informed decision that is best for your unique body. I believe that you should never be shamed for taking a medication.

My goal is to educate my clients about the medication, the potential side effects & teach them how to best nourish their body while taking these medications.

Muscle loss is common due to reduced appetite and lack of nourishment. It is key to ensure you are still eating enough consistently, eating enough protein and preserving muscle with strength training.

What is retatrutide?
• Triple-agonist peptide targeting GLP-1, GIP, and Glucagon receptors
• Designed to address obesity, cardiometabolic disease, and systemic inflammation

Retatrutide (Phase 3) — summary

What happened in the trials:
• People lost about 25–30% of their body weight
• That’s ~60–70+ lbs on average at the highest dose
• This is more weight loss than any GLP-1 drug so far
• Many people also had less joint pain and moved better

Side effects (what people actually felt):
• Mostly stomach-related: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation
• These were more common at higher doses
• About 1 in 5 people stopped the highest dose because of side effects

Is it safe (based on current data):
• No new major safety problems showed up in Phase 3
• Side effects looked similar to other GLP-1 drugs, just stronger
• Long-term safety is still being studied, but so far it looks acceptable for many people

What is GHK-Cu?
GHK-Cu is a naturally occurring copper complex first identified in human plasma in 1973. It is famous for its role in severe wound healing and tissue regeneration.
In our 20s, plasma levels of GHK-Cu are high. By age 60, they drop by over 60 percent, directly correlating with the visual and systemic signs of aging.
But researchers discovered it does much more than just heal skin.
panels.scene: Text-only panel explaining GHK-Cu's role in aging and healing

panels.subject: face_skin

The results
• Resets expression of ~4,000 human genes (nearly 30% of the genome) to a younger, healthier state
• Increases collagen and elastin production by up to 70%
• Stimulates blood vessel and nerve outgrowth
• Suppresses genes associated with cellular breakdown and inflammation
It literally tells aging cells to act young again.

Why Peptides Are So Well Received By The Body
Peptides aren’t foreign. They’re already part of you.
Natural Signaling Compounds – Peptides are short chains of amino acids that your body already uses to send messages—like telling your cells when to heal, grow, burn fat, or reduce inflammation.
Biodegradable + Bioidentical – Once they’ve done their job, most therapeutic peptides naturally break down into amino acids, the building blocks of protein—leaving no toxic residue behind.
Precision Over Suppression – Unlike pharmaceuticals that often override your system, peptides restore natural communication—helping your body do what it’s already designed to do, just better.
Fewer Side Effects – Because they work with your body (not against it), peptides are typically more gentle, well-tolerated, and targeted—making them an ideal tool in regenerative wellness.

How Peptides Are Delivered in the Body

Peptides are administered in ways that preserve their structure and effectiveness:

Injectable (Subcutaneous): Most common for deep tissue or systemic action (e.g., BPC-157, CJC/lpa).

Nasal Spray: For cognitive or neurological benefits (e.g., Semax, Selank).

Oral Capsules: Used for gut-specific peptides or stabilized molecules (e.g., oral BPC-157, KPv).

Topical Creams: For localized skin repair or joint support (e.g., GHK-Cu creams).

The delivery method matters — it determines how efficiently the peptide reaches its target.

WHAT PEPTIDES ACTUALLY ARE
(and why they're not as complicated as they sound)

Peptides are short chains of amino acids 💊
They already exist naturally in your body.

Their job is cell communication.
They help your cells recognize signals like:
• repair
• balance
• recovery
• metabolism

Think of peptides as tiny messengers that
tell your body where and how to respond
instead of forcing change.

That's why they tend to feel supportive, not extreme.
panels.scene: gym background with text overlay about peptides

panels.subject: body

Peptides don't override your system.
They plug into pathways your body already uses.

They help:
• speed up healing signals
• improve efficiency
• reduce "miscommunication" caused by stress, hormones, or aging

This is why the right peptide can feel subtle but powerful ✨

Yes — peptides are chains of amino acids, and your body naturally produces certain ones.
But most of the peptides being promoted online, specifically by influencers are NOT naturally occurring in the human body.

You know what? There is no magic and to lose weight you have to eat less than your daily needs.

You can also consume teas such as chamomile, green tea, black tea etc., or create some water with fruits like blueberries, cucumbers, strawberries etc

Why Women Respond Differently
Women naturally pulse GH more frequently than men do.
→ Higher baseline GH pulse frequency = different sensitivity
→ Estrogen amplifies GH receptor signaling
→ Lower endogenous IGF-1 means more room to benefit
→ Response shifts across the menstrual cycle
Same dose, different biology — women are not small men.

The Estrogen Connection
Estrogen and GH axis crosstalk is real and clinically relevant.

High Estrogen
Amplified GH pulse height
Greater IGF-1 lift
Higher fluid sensitivity

Low Estrogen
Blunted GH response
Slower visceral fat mobilization
Closer to male response pattern

Postmenopausal women without HRT may need dose adjustment.

Non-cancerous tumors that grow within the uterine walls and

SELANK - THE "CALM" PEPTIDE

What is it?
Selank is a synthetic peptide
developed in Russia, modeled
after the human immune
peptide tuftsin, and studied for
its anti-anxiety and
cognitive-supporting effects.

How does it work?
It modulates neurotransmitter pathways
involved in stress and cognition while
influencing neurotrophic signaling linked to
brain resilience and mental clarity.

What does the research say?
Clinical trials show Selank reduces anxiety in
patients with generalized anxiety disorder,
performing comparably to benzodiazepines
without sedation or dependence. Preclinical
studies link Selank to increased BDNF
expression and serotonin modulation,
mechanisms tied to mood, learning, and
stress adaptation.
panels.scene: Text card explaining Selank peptide's calming effects

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
SEMAX - "THE BRAIN BUILDER"

What is it?
Semax is a synthetic peptide
based on a fragment of
ACTH (a melanocortin
hormone), developed in Russia
and used/researched for
neuroprotection and cognitive support—
especially in stroke-related contexts.

How does it work?
It appears to upregulate neurotrophic
signaling (notably BDNF/NGF pathways) and
shift brain gene expression toward less
inflammation + better neurotransmission,
which is why it's studied for focus, learning,
and recovery.

What does the research say?
Evidence is strongest for

clinically in Russia for this). Semax turns on
brain growth signals and downshifts
neuroinflammation.

CEREBROLYSIN - "PROTECT-IDE"

What is it?
Cerebrolysin is a neurotrophic peptide complex derived from purified porcine brain proteins, used clinically in parts of Europe and Asia for brain repair and cognitive recovery.

How does it work?
It delivers BDNF- and NGF-like peptides that support neuronal survival, plasticity, and synaptic repair, while helping shift the brain out of a chronic inflammatory state.

What does the research say?
Human studies in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and neurodegenerative disease show Cerebrolysin can improve cognitive function and neurological recovery. Its effects are linked to enhanced neuroplasticity, reduced neuroinflammation, and protection against neuronal loss.

DIHEXA - "EINSTEIN" PEPTIDE

What is it?
Dihexa is a synthetic peptide
nootropic derived from
angiotensin IV, designed to
strongly support synaptic
growth and memory formation.

How does it work?
It activates the HGF/c-Met pathway, a key
driver of synaptogenesis, essentially
enhancing the brain's ability to form and
strengthen neural connections.

What does the research say?
Preclinical studies show Dihexa dramatically
improves learning and memory in animal
models, even reversing cognitive deficits. Its
effects are linked to rapid synapse formation,
making it one of the most potent
synaptogenic compounds studied, though
human data is still limited.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Demand for peptides has exploded as influencers flood social media with promises of sculpted physiques, glowing skin, rapidly healing injuries and youthful energy.

The demand has given rise to a burgeoning gray market, where wellness spas, multilevel marketers and telehealth websites ply the public with vials of "research grade" peptides labeled "not for human use."

Ads on Meta platforms claim peptide users can get a range of health benefits.
panels.scene: Text panel explaining peptide market explosion and gray market

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Kennedy, who described himself
as a "big fan" of peptides, said the
FDA acted illegally.

But three former FDA officials
familiar with how the agency
created the criteria to assess the
peptides in the first place say
Kennedy has mischaracterized
their work and that the agency's
decision to ban certain peptides
was supported by numerous
documented safety concerns.

If Kennedy reverses their decision,
it would give a false imprimatur
of safety to more than a dozen
unapproved, untested drugs, the
officials said.
panels.scene: Text panel discussing FDA peptide regulations and safety concerns.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
In 2023, the FDA deemed 19 peptide drugs too unsafe to be dispensed by compounding pharmacies, which mix components of approved drugs to create bespoke medication for people who have trouble taking commonly available products.

Now, under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the agency is poised to reverse itself.

That's despite few clinical studies supporting the effectiveness or safety of these peptides.
panels.scene: Text panel detailing FDA peptide drug policy change

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
The Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding, one of the largest industry associations lobbying for the FDA to change its stance on peptides, acknowledges it knows little about the safety of individual peptides being sold to the public.

The group argues the public would be safer if peptides were handled by regulated compounding pharmacies instead of the gray market and that the FDA should forgo the usual human clinical trials in order to bring about this shift.
panels.scene: Text panel discussing peptide safety and FDA lobbying

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
Newer FDA-approved peptide drugs such as semaglutide and tirzepatide — broadly known as GLP-1s — have exploded in popularity for weight loss.

The popularity of these drugs has made the public more comfortable with injectables and has helped drive attention to other gray-market peptides.
panels.scene: TV screens showing GLP-1 drug commercial in bar

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Kennedy wasn't clear on exactly how the FDA would let compounders start dispensing peptides, describing it only as "some kind of action" to make "about 14" peptides "more accessible." Nor has he specified which peptides he wants to make available. (Neither the FDA nor HHS responded to ProPublica's requests for more information.)

But several regulatory shortcuts exist and, ultimately, Kennedy could simply declare the ingredients are legal.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Similar to CJC, Ipamorelin stimulates the pituitary to release growth hormone (GH) but through different pathways. Specifically, Ipamorelin mimics a natural hunger hormone called ghrelin which binds to growth hormone secretagogue receptors (GHS-R) in the pituitary gland and hypothalamus.

Basically, it mimics your body's natural production of GH, releasing GH in short bursts much like your body would do on its own, especially during sleep or post-workout. Unlike GHRPs like GHRP-6 or GHRP-2, Ipamorelin is very selective as it only triggers GH release without spiking cortisol or prolactin.

Ipamorelin is also commonly stacked with CJC-1295, a GHRH (GHRH is the actual signal that starts the GH release process) Peptide due to their synergy as the two work together to boost both the intensity and frequency of growth hormone, all through different pathways to prevent overstimulation. This leads to higher OGF-1 levels downstream which supports muscle growth, fat burning, tissue repair, all while keeping the hormonal balance clean and stable.

What is a peptide?
A peptide is a small chain of amino acids, which are
the building blocks of proteins.

Think of it simply like this:
A peptide is a short piece of a protein that sends
signals in the body.

These signals can tell your body to do things like:
-Build muscle
-Burn fat
-Heal tissue
-Produce hormones
-Improve skin or hair
So in simple terms:
Peptides are tiny messenger molecules that tell
your body how to function better.

CJC-1295 Basics
What it does:
- Stimulates pulsatile GH
- release from pituitary
- Increases IGF-1 levels
- Promotes muscle growth & recovery
- Supports fat loss & metabolism
- Improves sleep quality and skin health
Explanation:
CJC-1295 is a synthetic GHRH analog that
mimics natural growth hormone pulses,
binding to GHRH receptors to
stimulate sustained GH release from the
pituitary gland.
IGF-1 drives effects:
- Muscle growth
- Bone density
- Tissue repair

CJC-1295 also extends GH half-life via
conjugation with DAC, reducing clearance by
the kindneys.

- Alters GH/IGF-1 axis
- Affects metabolism and fluid balance.
What to do:
- Monitor dosage carefully and track side effects.
Common side effects:
- Injection site reactions
- Flushing or warmth
- Water retention
- Headaches/dizznous
- Joint discomfort
- Increased hunger
- Temporary insulin sensitvity changes.

Peptides are short chains of amino acids.

Your body already produces them naturally

do and when to do it.

For example, some peptides signal hunger,
while others signal recovery or fat
metabolism.

panels.ocrText:
Hey SO I've officially lost 100 pounds. Crazy.

Last year I got diagnosed with a rare-ish condition called Spinal Epidural Lipomatosis (SEL) where fat tissue accumulates in the spinal column, causing pain, mobility issues and eventually irreparable nerve damage. In my case, nerve damage had already started to set in, and my mobility was severely limited. The shitty thing about SEL is that there isn't much you can do about it besides completely overhaul your entire life to stop it from progressing. So I did.

As somebody who is quite visible online, people have started noticing my weight loss and asking/messaging me about it, and so I want to talk about it here, openly and honestly.
panels.scene: Text-only panel sharing personal weight loss journey

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
Like many fat women, I was dismissed and ignored when I went to seek out medical care for the searing pain that would shoot down my back and into my hips and thighs. I wasn't even told I had SEL by my doctor, I had to read it in the notes in MyChart: it *can sometimes be* related to obesity, so what was the point of telling me? Of course it was my fault for having a rare disorder that deposits fat in my spine.

But two things can be true at the same time-while I struggled, it is also true that I wasn't healthy. As a result of repeated injury, I became sedentary. I would get winded walking up the stairs and exhausted walking around the block. I would eat to comfort myself, I would eat to soothe, I would eat because I was bored, I would eat because I couldn't tell if I was hungry or not, and the cycle of further limited mobility would continue

panels.ocrText:
optimal ghk-cu protocol

titration

Follow a step-up titration model to find your effective maintenance dose while minimizing side effects:

Week 1-2: 1 mg/day — establish baseline tolerance. Track injection site reactions, energy levels, sleep quality, and any GI disturbance daily.

Week 3-4: 1.5 mg/day — if no adverse reactions at 1 mg, increase by 0.5 mg. This is where most users begin noticing subtle skin texture improvements and accelerated wound healing.

Week 5+: 2 mg/day maintenance — the practical ceiling for subcutaneous GHK-Cu. Doses above 2 mg/day show diminishing returns in community reports and increase the likelihood of nausea and copper-related GI discomfort.

Key signals to watch during titration: injection site reactions (should stay mild), GI disturbance (nausea, metallic taste), and hair shedding patterns. A brief telogen effluvium in weeks 2-5 is a known transient effect — it resolves and often precedes improved regrowth.
panels.scene: Text-based guide for GHK-Cu dosage titration protocol

panels.subject: face_skin
panels.ocrText:
optimal ghk-cu protocol
what is GHK-Cu
GHK-Cu (glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine copper complex) is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide first isolated from human plasma by Loren Pickart in 1973. It is one of the most extensively studied regenerative peptides in dermatology and wound-healing literature.
Plasma concentrations average ~200 mcg/L at age 20, declining to ~80 mcg/L by age 60 — a 60% drop that parallels visible skin aging. Exogenous supplementation aims to restore youthful signaling levels.
GHK-Cu upregulates collagen I, collagen III, and elastin synthesis while modulating matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) remodeling pathways. Genome-wide studies show it influences the expression of over 4,000 genes, including anti-inflammatory cascades — suppressing IL-6 and TNF-alpha — and pro-repair pathways involving TGF-beta and VEGF.
Its dual role as both a copper delivery vehicle and a signaling molecule makes it unique among peptides: the copper ion catalyzes superoxide dismutase activity while the tripeptide backbone drives receptor-mediated gene expression changes.
Fig. 1A — Skin before and after peptide-based treatment course. PMC3149480.
Fig. 1B — GHK-Cu molecular structure. Source: PubChem, NIH/NLM.
panels.scene: Text-heavy slide explaining GHK-Cu's benefits and science

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
optimal ghk-cu protocol
how to inject
Route: subcutaneous injection. GHK-Cu is a small tripeptide (molecular weight
~403 Da) with excellent subcutaneous bioavailability. Intramuscular is
unnecessary and increases bruising risk.
Equipment: 29-31 gauge insulin syringe, 0.5-inch needle. The smaller the gauge,
the less injection site irritation — 31G is preferred for daily use.
Injection sites (rotate daily): lower abdomen (2+ inches from navel), upper outer
thigh, posterior upper arm. Consistent rotation prevents lipodystrophy and reduces
cumulative injection site reactions.
Reconstitution: inject bacteriostatic water slowly down the vial wall. Swirl gently
— never shake. GHK-Cu dissolves readily at room temperature within 30-60
seconds.
Storage: refrigerate reconstituted vials at 2-8°C. Use within 21-28 days of
reconstitution. Do not freeze. Discard if solution becomes cloudy or develops
particulates. Keep lyophilized (unreconstituted) vials at room temperature away
from light.
Fig. 4A — Subcutaneous injection technique. PMC5225387.
Fig. 4B — Insulin syringe delivery and injection site detail. PMC5225387.
panels.scene: Text-only guide for injecting GHK-Cu with diagrams

panels.subject: face_skin
panels.ocrText:
optimal ghk-cu protocol

cycle length

The standard cycle structure is 8-12 weeks on, 4 weeks off. This balances cumulative collagen synthesis gains against receptor desensitization and copper homeostasis.

Collagen synthesis timeline: measurable upregulation begins by week 2-3. Visible results (skin texture, wound healing speed, nail quality) typically emerge at week 4-6. Peak collagen deposition occurs at week 8-10, which is why cutting cycles short at 6 weeks leaves significant gains on the table.

Off-cycle rationale: the 4-week break allows receptor resensitization, copper level normalization, and prevents chronic copper accumulation. Serum copper and ceruloplasmin should return to baseline within 2-3 weeks off.

Hair-focused protocols may extend to 12-16 weeks because hair follicle cycling operates on longer timescales than dermal collagen turnover. The telogen-to-anagen transition takes 8-12 weeks minimum.

Plan 2-3 full cycles per year. Most users report cumulative improvements across cycles, with the strongest visible results emerging after the second cycle.
panels.scene: Text-based skincare protocol guide for GHK-Cu treatment cycles

panels.subject: face_skin
panels.ocrText:
optimal ghk-cu protocol
starting dose
The standard subcutaneous starting dose is 1 mg/day, administered once daily.
This aligns with the dose range most commonly reported in community protocols
and is consistent with the concentrations shown to upregulate collagen gene
expression in vitro.
Reconstitution: dissolve a 5 mg vial in 2.5 mL bacteriostatic water to yield a
concentration of 2 mg/mL. Draw 0.5 mL (50 units on an insulin syringe) for a 1 mg
dose. Swirl gently — do not shake, as GHK-Cu is a relatively fragile tripeptide.
For sensitive individuals or those new to injectable peptides, a conservative start
of 0.5 mg/day for 5-7 days allows assessment of injection site tolerance and any
copper-related GI sensitivity before moving to the full 1 mg dose.
Monitor injection site reactions closely during the first week. Mild erythema lasting
1-3 hours is normal and expected. Persistent welts or spreading redness beyond
4+ hours warrants dose reduction.
panels.scene: Text-based guide for GHK-Cu peptide dosage and reconstitution.

panels.subject: face_skin
panels.ocrText:
optimal ghk-cu protocol
stack: nutrition and training

GHK-Cu does not work in isolation. Collagen synthesis requires specific cofactors,
and stacking them correctly amplifies results significantly:

Vitamin C 500-1000 mg/day — essential hydroxylation cofactor for procollagen.
Without adequate vitamin C, collagen cross-linking fails regardless of GHK-Cu
dose. Split doses (morning + evening) optimize plasma levels.

Glycine 5-10 g/day — the most abundant amino acid in collagen (every third
residue). Most people are glycine-deficient relative to collagen synthesis demands.
Take with meals or in a pre-bed shake.

Collagen hydrolysate 10-15 g/day — provides proline and hydroxyproline
directly. Hydrolyzed collagen peptides are absorbed intact and signal fibroblast
collagen production independently of GHK-Cu.

Zinc 15-25 mg/day — supports wound healing and immune function, but do not
exceed 40 mg/day. Excess zinc competes with copper absorption, directly
undermining GHK-Cu efficacy.

Microneedling 0.5-1.0 mm with topical GHK-Cu applied immediately post-
needling synergizes powerfully — the microchannels bypass the stratum
corneum, delivering GHK-Cu directly to the dermal layer where fibroblasts reside.

Peptide Safety Guide
Simple Cheat Sheet
• Start With ONE Peptide – try a single
peptide for the first 2 weeks so you know
exactly what helps or harms
• Add New Compounds Slowly – introduce
another peptide only after you’re sure
the first is safe
• Keep It Clean – wipe vial/skin, mix with
bacteriostatic water, swirl softly
• Keep It Cold – store mixed vials in the
fridge; toss after 4 weeks
• Switch Shot Spots – belly, thigh, tricep,
upper glute; avoids lumps & soreness
• Safe Needle Trash – drop used needles
in a “sharps” box, not the trash can
• Check Your Blood – get basic labs every
month to be sure organs are happy
• Watch Your Meds – insulin, blood-
pressure pills, antidepressants may need
dose tweaks
• Stop if Allergic – rash, swelling, tight
chest? Quit and call your doctor

IMPORTANT NOTICE

This carousel contains clinical images that some viewers may find distressing.
The photographs document one individual's journey with Acne Keloidalis Nuchae (AKN) and are shared to educate, raise awareness and provide educational context.

THE 7-STEP PROTOCOL
① TEMPERATURE FIRST Let peptide vial AND BAC water reach room
temperature (15-30 min) Cold + cold = cloudiness risk
② SANITIZE EVERYTHING Alcohol swab on both vial stoppers. Let dry
completely.
③ EQUALIZE PRESSURE Insert empty syringe to release vacuum
(lyophilization creates pressure difference)
④ DRAW SLOWLY Typical ratios: 1-2mL BAC per 5mg peptide Use peptide
calculator for exact amounts
⑤ AIM AT THE WALL Inject solvent down the SIDE of the vial NEVER blast
directly onto powder
⑥ SWIRL, DON'T SHAKE Gently roll between palms. Let sit 5-10 min.
Shaking = denaturation = ruined peptide
⑦ VERIFY CLARITY Solution should be crystal clear Cloudiness = DO NOT
USE (unless AOD/HGH Frag)
Source: Particle Peptides Calculator Guide; Verified Peptides Best Practices

panels.subject: other

CLOUDY VIAL = RUINED PEPTIDE
That $150 vial you just bought? One wrong move during reconstitution and it's expensive garbage.
What causes cloudiness: → Wrong solvent for the peptide type → Temperature shock (cold solution + cold vial) → Shaking or blasting water directly onto powder → Peptide denaturation/aggregation
The rule: If your solution looks milky, has particles, or won't clear up, DO NOT INJECT. You've denatured the peptide structure.
Source: PMC10056213 - "Peptide aggregation and precipitation indicates physical instability and compromised bioactivity"

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
KNOW YOUR PEPTIDE TYPE
HYDROPHILIC (Water-Loving)
Dissolve easily in BAC water

These peptides have amino acid sequences that attract water
molecules. They contain charged or polar residues that make them
naturally soluble in aqueous solutions.

Examples: BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu, Retatrutide, CJC-1295,
Ipamorelin, Semax, Selank

HYDROPHOBIC (Water-Resistant)
Need acidic solutions or organic solvents

Peptides with 50%+ hydrophobic residues (Trp, Leu, Ile, Phe, Met,
Val, Tyr) are poorly soluble in water. They require acidic
environments or co-solvents.

Examples: IGF-1 LR3, IGF-1 DES, HGH Fragment 176-191 (AOD-9604)

Source: SB-Peptide Solubility Guidelines; PMC5665799

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
STOP DOING THIS
× SHAKING THE VIAL
Creates foam at air-liquid interface. This denatures peptide bonds and causes aggregation. Your "mixed" peptide is now broken peptide.
× BLASTING WATER ONTO POWDER
The force shears fragile peptide chains and causes them to stick to vial walls. Always aim at the glass wall and let it trickle down.
× MIXING COLD + COLD
Temperature shock causes precipitation. Both vial and solvent must reach room temp first.
× USING TAP WATER OR NON-STERILE SOLUTIONS
Introduces bacteria and mineral contaminants that degrade peptides within hours.
× STORING IN REFRIGERATOR DOOR
Temperature fluctuations from opening/closing accelerate degradation. Store in back of fridge.
× MIXING INCOMPATIBLE PEPTIDES
BPC-157 (15 amino acids) + TB-500 (43 amino acids) = different pH requirements = precipitation. Keep them separate.
Source: PMC10056213; UK Peptides Reconstitution Guide; Peptide Source Forum

Weight Loss Peptides (GLP-1s)
Examples: Semaglutide (Ozempic,
Wegovy), Tirzepatide (Mounjaro
— also a GIP agonist), Liraglutide
(Saxenda, Victoza), Dulaglutide
(Trulicity).
GLP-1 is a hormone your gut releases
after eating.
Its job is to help regulate blood sugar and
appetite by:
•Increasing insulin secretion (when
blood sugar is high)
• Decreasing glucagon secretion
(which prevents your liver from dumping
more sugar into your blood)
• Slowing stomach emptying (you
feel full longer)
• Acting on the brain to reduce
hunger
Scientists created synthetic versions that
last much longer in the body.

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
CJC-1295 is a synthetic peptide designed to stimulate your body's natural production of growth hormone.

Growth hormone, as the name suggests, is a hormone crucial for muscle growth, metabolism, and bone development during puberty.

However, recently it's been advertised as a safe way to increase height, bone density, and muscle mass.

But how does it actually work? And is it safe?

4 months on peptides + mk677
same angle btw

4 months on peptides + mk677
same angle btw
panels.scene: Before and after photos of same person showing physical changes.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
So what is better?

CJC-1295 without DAC
will ultimately be safer
long-term due to the fact
that it mimics your body's
natural GH pattern but at
the cost of requiring
multiple injections.

CJC-1295 without DAC
will be a better option for
people who don't have the
time to inject often or want
more effects but be aware
that the constant release
of GH means a larger
window for side effects
including the risk of
desensitization (next slide
for more info).
panels.scene: Text-only panel comparing CJC-1295 variants

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
CJC-1295 is a synthetic version of GHRH. When injected, it binds to the same receptors in the pituitary gland that natural GHRH uses. This causes your body to release more GH in a pulsatile pattern, mimicking your body's natural production of GH rather than flooding it all at once like synthetic HGH injections (will be covered in another video).

If your growth plates are open, this can contribute to additional height, bone growth, and bone density but this will all be determined by how your body reacts to it (everyone is different, some are genetic hyper-responders).
panels.scene: Text panel explaining CJC-1295 effects on growth and GH release.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
However, there are
variations of CJC-1295
which you should be
familiar with.

CJC-1295 with DAC (Drug
Affinity Complex) is a
modification that makes
the peptide bind to a
protein in your blood called
albumin, which protects it
from being broken down
too quickly. This allows it
to stay active in your body
for up to a week,
stimulating GH release
over a longer period of
time with just one
injection.

CJC-1295 without DAC
(also known as Mod-GRF
1-29) doesn't bind to
albumin, so it clears from
the body much faster. It's
typically used daily and
gives shorter, more
controlled pulses of GH.

Both versions stimulate
GH which leads to IGF-1
which drives growth and
recovery. The main
difference is how long they
act and how often they
need to be taken.
panels.scene: Text-only panel explaining CJC-1295 variations

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
To understand how
CJC-1295 works, you first
need to know how your
body naturally produces
growth hormone (GH).

Normally, your
hypothalamus releases a
peptide called GHRH aka
Growth Hormone
Releasing Hormone. This
then signals the pituitary
gland, a small organ at the
base of your brain, to
produce growth hormone
in short pulses, mostly at
night while you sleep.

GH then travels through
your bloodstream and
reaches the liver, where it
stimulates the production
of IGF-1 (Insulin Growth
Factor 1), a hormone
responsible for most of the
body's growth and repair
functions.
panels.scene: Text explaining CJC-1295's natural hormone production process

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Desensitization happens
when your body stops
responding to a signal
because it's
overstimulated for too
long.

When you use something
like CJC-1295 too
frequently or at a too high
dose, your pituitary gland
can become less sensitive
to it. The receptors that
respond to CJC/GHRH
downregulate, meaning
they get used to the signal
and stop reacting as
strongly. As a result, GH
release declines, even
even though you're still taking
the peptide.

Think of it like a car alarm
going off constantly. At
first, everyone notices. But
after a while, people start
tuning it out. Your pituitary
works the same way.
panels.scene: Text-only panel explaining desensitization with CJC-1295 analogy

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
How do you prevent this?

Use proper dosing
protocols: Don't overuse
CJC-1295. Stick to
recommended doses.

Use CJC with Ipamorelin
(or another GHRP): I will go
into this more in the next
video but combining a
GHRP analog like CJC with
a GHRP (growth hormone
releasing peptide) like
Ipamorelin gives a
synergistic pulse without
overstimulating one
pathway too hard.

Cycle Usage: Use peptides
in on/off cycles. A
common method is 5 days
on 2 days off or 8-12
weeks on 2-4 weeks off to
give your receptors time to
recalibrate.

Monitor IGF-1 or GH levels
(if medically supervised): If
you notice effects fading
over time, lab work can
help you determine
whether your response is
turning off but if you don't
blast and follow a proper
cycle you most likely won't
need to do this.

WHAT HAPPENED
A fourteen-member
FDA advisory panel
voted on seven

The Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee met at
FDA's White Oak campus to decide whether each peptide
should be recommended for the 503A Bulks List.

That list is what allows a licensed compounding pharmacy to
legally prepare a substance from raw ingredient when there is
no FDA-approved product and no USP monograph behind it.

Each peptide was voted on twice — once for the free base
form, once for the acetate salt.

READ THIS PART TWICE

What this vote is not.

— Not FDA approval
None of these became approved drugs. Approval requires the kind of large controlled trials none of them have run.

— Not binding
The committee advises. FDA decides. The agency usually follows its panels — but it is not required to, and it has gone the other way before.

— Not a change you will see this week
Nothing about legal access shifts today. Formal rulemaking with public comment comes next, and that runs months to years.

@DRKRISTI.SAWICKI

recommended against every single one — citing inconsistent
chemical characterization, missing quality data, and human
evidence that was absent, small, or contradictory.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
SO WHAT DOES IT MEAN
A legal pathway
opened — slightly.
All seven had already come off the Category 2 "may not be
compounded" list back in April. That is what made this review
possible in the first place.
A yes vote moves each one toward the list a 503A pharmacy
can actually compound from with a prescription. If FDA agrees
and finishes rulemaking, sourcing moves from the grey market
to a licensed pharmacy that tests each batch for potency,
purity, and sterility.
Providing access through a medically supervised
route is the win.
@DRKRISTI.SAWICKI

FDA reviews
The agency weighs the votes, the panel discussion, and roughly
1,860 public docket comments.

NEXT
Proposed rule
If FDA acts, it publishes a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking with
another public comment window.

THEN
Final rule
Only after a final rule amends 21 CFR 216.23 can pharmacies
legally compound from these. Realistically 2027 or later.

ALSO
Round two
The committee is scheduled to meet again before the end of
February 2027 on the remaining nominated peptides.

HUMAN DATA (SO FAR)
Extremely limited human findings:
1. Intra-Articular Knee Pain Study (2021) - PMID 34324435
a.Single study: 12 patients receiving intra-articular BPC-157
for chronic knee pain
b.58% (7/12) reported pain relief >6 months
c. Major limitations: No control group, retrospective
design, small sample size, unspecified pain etiology
2. Interstitial Cystitis Study (2024) - PMID 39325560
a.Pilot study: 12 women with interstitial cystitis refractory to
pentosan polysulfate received 10mg BPC-157
b.83% (10/12) reported 100% symptom resolution, 17% (2/12)
reported 80% resolution, no adverse events reported
c. Major limitations: No control/placebo group, small
sample size, no long-term follow up
3. IV Safety/Pharmacokinetic Study (2025) - PMID 40131143
a.Single study: 2 patients receiving BPC-157 intravenously,
Day 1 (10mg) and Day 2 (20mg)
b.No measurable effects on vitals or tested biomarkers of
heart, liver, kidney, thyroid or blood glucose levels. No
side effects reported
c. Major limitations: Small sample size, no long-term
follow up, generalizability (2 healthy adults)

1 Injecting BAC Water Too Fast
When reconstituting peptides:
X Don't blast the water directly onto the powder
✓ Let the BAC water slowly run down the inside wall of the vial

Some peptides are delicate and excessive agitation can affect stability.
Slow and gentle wins.

2 Shaking The Vial
X Don't shake
✓ Gently swirl or roll between your fingers

Many peptides dissolve naturally within a few minutes.
Shaking creates unnecessary agitation and can damage fragile peptide structures.

3 Leaving It In Heat Or Sunlight
Heat, light, and temperature swings are peptide enemies.
✓ Store reconstituted peptides in the refrigerator
✓ Keep away from direct sunlight
✓ Return to the fridge after use

BAC WATER

BAC water contains benzyl alcohol, which helps reduce bacterial growth after multiple punctures.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
The biggest one is insulin. When you eat carbs, blood sugar rises, insulin gets released, and insulin activates somatostatin, the brake pedal on GH release from your pituitary.
The peptide is trying to trigger a GH pulse from your pituitary. Insulin activates the exact brake system that suppresses that pulse. Your last meal is working directly against the signal.
This is why carbs before injection are the worst offender. They trigger insulin, which reactivates the exact pathway that blocks GH from releasing.
panels.scene: Doctor explains insulin's effect on growth hormone release.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
No carbs or fat for at least 90 minutes before injection. If you already ate, wait at least an hour and a half to two hours before dosing.

After injection, wait at least 30 minutes before eating carbs or fat. Your first GH pulse hits around 20 to 30 minutes post-injection, and you want that window clear of those macronutrients.

The best timing is first thing in the morning on an empty stomach or at bedtime, at least two hours after your last meal. If you are dosing twice a day, space them about three hours apart so your pituitary can reset for another pulse.
panels.scene: Text-only panel with medical advice on growth hormone injection timing

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
Elevated blood sugar also suppresses GH release on its own, through a separate mechanism that has nothing to do with insulin or somatostatin. One carb meal hits you two ways.
Dietary fat creates a third problem. When you eat fat, free fatty acids rise in your blood, and those fatty acids independently blunt GH pulsing without any insulin involvement.
Protein is the one exception. It has a minimal effect on insulin's ability to suppress somatostatin and does not raise blood sugar or free fatty acids the same way. It is the only macronutrient you can eat close to injection time without major blunting.
panels.scene: Doctor explains hormone impact of diet macros

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
Growth hormone peptides are designed to trigger your pituitary gland to release GH in a pulse. That pulse is how your body burns fat, repairs tissue, and builds muscle while you sleep.

The recommendation to take them fasted is not arbitrary. Three things that show up in your bloodstream after a meal directly suppress that GH pulse, and each one works through a different mechanism.

You can still get some GH release if you eat beforehand, but the size of the pulse drops significantly. You are paying for the peptide and getting a fraction of the output.
panels.scene: Doctor explains growth hormone peptide usage and fasting benefits

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
Growth hormone peptides need a clean metabolic window to do their job. Insulin, glucose, and free fatty acids each suppress the GH pulse through a different pathway.
Fasting before injection is not about discipline or optimization culture. It is about removing the three things that directly fight the peptide you are taking.
If you are using growth hormone peptides and not seeing the results you expected, check your timing and what you ate beforehand. The peptide might be working fine. Your blood just was not ready for it.

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
Four: their metabolism unlocks. Your body is supposed to flip between burning sugar and burning fat depending on what you need. When GH drops, that switch gets stuck.
You store more fat, burn less of it, and your energy crashes between meals even when you are eating enough. The same diet and exercise that worked at 35 stops producing results, and it is not a willpower problem.
GH peptides wake up the fat-burning machinery that went quiet. Women on them report steadier energy through the day and less need to eat every two hours just to keep going.
5 / 7→
panels.scene: Doctor explains metabolic changes with GH peptides.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
One: they sleep deeper. Your body releases roughly 60% of its daily growth hormone during deep sleep, and that number drops every year after 35. Most women over 40 notice sleep falling apart before anything else.
As estrogen fluctuates in perimenopause, your deep sleep gets shorter and your GH pulses shrink with it. Less deep sleep means less GH, and less GH means worse sleep. The cycle feeds itself.
GH peptides trigger a pulse that mirrors your body's natural nighttime pattern. Women who start them consistently report falling asleep faster and staying asleep through the night.
2 / 7→
panels.scene: Doctor explains hormone impact on sleep quality.

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
Five: they hold onto muscle. Women lose roughly 3 to 8% of lean mass per decade, and that rate speeds up during perimenopause when GH, estrogen, and IGF-1 all drop at the same time.

Growth hormone tells your muscle fibers to repair and rebuild after every training session. When GH drops, your muscles recover slower, build less new tissue, and break down faster between workouts.

GH peptides bring back the signal your muscles need to respond to training. Faster recovery and visible changes in muscle tone are some of the things women notice earliest.
panels.scene: Text-only panel explaining muscle loss and GH peptides for women

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
These are not five separate problems. They are five
symptoms of the same biology: growth hormone
production dropping as you move through
perimenopause and beyond.
There are many GH peptides available, each with
different benefits and trade-offs. Finding the right one for
you means matching the compound to your goals,
managing side effects, and dialing in injection frequency
and timing.
The biology is well understood, the tools exist, and the
research on women's GH axis keeps growing. The
conversation is worth having sooner than most women	hink.
Got a question? Leave it below. Peptides, hormones, or
anything else you're curious about. I reply to all of them.
panels.scene: Doctor explains growth hormone decline symptoms

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY
Two: the brain fog clears. Your brain runs a waste-
clearance system called the glymphatic system, and
growth hormone is what powers it. When GH drops, that
cleanup slows down and metabolic waste builds up
between your neurons.
During deep sleep, fluid flows through your brain and
flushes out protein fragments and cellular debris that
accumulate during the day. Growth hormone drives that
process. Without it, the waste just sits there.
When GH output comes back up, so does the overnight
clearance. Sharper thinking and faster recall are two of
the earliest things women report, sometimes within the
first few weeks.
panels.scene: Doctor explains brain fog and growth hormone effects

panels.subject: body
panels.ocrText:
GABRIEL ALIZAIDY MD, MS
@GABRIELALIZAIDY

Three: belly fat finally moves. You eat clean, train hard,
and still watch fat build around your midsection. That is
visceral fat, and it wraps around your organs where you
cannot see it.

An enzyme called hormone-sensitive lipase sits inside
those visceral fat cells. Its job is to break stored fat into
fuel your body can burn. Certain GH peptides activate
that enzyme and go after belly fat at the source.

In a 52-week controlled trial, visceral fat dropped 18%
while subcutaneous fat and lean mass stayed intact. The
peptide only went after the deep belly fat, not the rest of
your body composition.

panels.ocrText: Remember: Every body is different, so the weight loss plan that works for your friend may not work for you. PEPTIDE SCIENCE SERIES | 04
How Hormone Therapy Works
Hormone replacement therapy works by replenishing what the body is no longer producing in sufficient quantities.
When testosterone, estrogen, or thyroid hormone levels drop — due to age, injury, or illness — HRT delivers those hormones directly, restoring systemic balance quickly.
RESULTS CAN BE FELT WITHIN WEEKS.
However, because you're introducing exogenous hormones, your body often responds by reducing or stopping its own production altogether.
This suppression of the HPG axis is why HRT tends to become a long-term or permanent commitment, requiring ongoing physician monitoring and regular bloodwork to avoid imbalance.
KEY CONSIDERATIONS
REPLENISHES HORMONES DIRECTLY
Restores what the body isn't producing.
FAST ACTING
Relief and improvements can be felt within weeks.
SUPPRESSES NATURAL PRODUCTION
The body reduces or stops its own hormone output.
LONG-TERM COMMITMENT
HRT is typically a long-term or lifelong approach.
REQUIRES MONITORING
Physician oversight and regular bloodwork are essential for safety and balance.
HRT replaces hormones. Peptides stimulate your body to make them.
Different approaches. Different mechanisms. Different commitments.

How Peptides Work

Peptides work by stimulating your
hypothalamic-pituitary axis — the
command center of your endocrine system.

When you use a peptide like CJC-1295

This preserves your natural feedback loops,

Because they target specific pathways,

PEPTIDE SCIENCE SERIES | 06
The Verdict
For optimization, peptides win.
For clinical deficiency, HRT wins.
The mistake most people make is reaching for the sledgehammer — hormone replacement — when the situation calls for a scalpel.
If your labs are in range but you’re still dealing with slow recovery, poor sleep, body composition changes, or low energy, peptides are where you start.
If bloodwork confirms a genuine deficiency, HRT becomes a necessary tool.
In advanced cases, both can be stacked strategically.
Know your baseline, know your goal, and choose the tool that matches the problem.

01 Nausea (~40%)
The dominant side effect in RECONNECT. Often dose-dependent. Many users describe it as significant on first doses, attenuating with repeat exposure.

Vasomotor symptoms. Common in the first hour post-injection.

MC1R cross-activity (it's still a melanocortin agonist). Long-term users report changes; mole monitoring is reasonable.

PEPTIDES VS STEROIDS VS HORMONES
THE COMPLETE BREAKDOWN
OSHAMAH D GREAT
1. WHAT ARE HORMONES?
Hormones are the body's messenger system.
They are natural chemical messengers produced by glands that travel through the bloodstream to organs and tissues to regulate essential functions.

THEY REGULATE:
Metabolism
Libido & Fertility
Muscle Growth
Sleep
Stress
Mood
Hunger
Recovery
Energy

EXAMPLES OF HORMONES:
Testosterone
Estrogen
Insulin
Cortisol
etc.

IMPORTANT:
Hormones are a broad category.
Both peptides and steroids can involve hormones.

2. WHAT ARE PEPTIDES?
Peptides are short chains of amino acids.

They act as signaling molecules or messengers.

PEPTIDES USUALLY:
✓ Signal the body
✓ Regulate processes
✓ Trigger the release of hormones
✓ Improve healing & repair
✓ Influence specific pathways
✓ Target very specific functions

SIMPLE WAY TO UNDERSTAND:
Peptides are often INSTRUCTIONS, not raw force.

EXAMPLES:
CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin
Signal your body to release more of its own growth hormone (HGH).

GLP-1 Peptides
(Semaglutide, Tirzepatide, etc.)
Help regulate hunger, insulin response, blood sugar & satiety.

3. WHAT ARE STEROIDS?
Steroids are compounds built from a cholesterol-based structure.

Most anabolic steroids are designed to DIRECTLY MIMIC TESTOSTERONE.

STERIODS USUALLY:
✗ Replace or overpower the system
✗ Act directly on hormone receptors
✗ Often shut down natural production
✗ Produce more forceful effects
✗ Carry higher risk of side effects
✗ Are not signaling the body—they take over the function

EXAMPLE:
Testosterone Injections
Directly increase testosterone levels.
The body senses high levels and may shut down natural production.

Ipamorelin
Ipamorelin is a synthetic peptide classified as a growth hormone
secretagogues (GHS). It acts as a ghrelin mimetic by binding to
the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a),
stimulating the pituitary gland to release growth hormone (GH)
in a more natural pulsatile pattern.

KEY POINTS
• It is considered relatively selective compared
with older GH-releasing peptides, with less
effect on cortisol and prolactin levels.
• Research interest includes:
臀 Body composition and fat metabolism
🏃‍♂️ Exercise recovery and tissue repair
🌙 Sleep quality
🦴 Bone and connective tissue health
➕ Postoperative recovery models
• Human evidence remains limited. Most
published data are early-phase trials or
animal studies, and long-term safety
data are lacking.
• It is not approved by the FDA or EMA for
general medical use, and many products
sold online are marketed as
"research use only."

MECHANISM OF ACTION
Ipamorelin → GHS-R1a activation → GH release
By activating GHS-R1a, ipamorelin stimulates the pituitary
gland to release growth hormone (GH) in a natural,
pulsatile pattern.

POTENTIAL AREAS OF INTEREST
• Improving body composition
• Boosting metabolism
• Accelerating tissue repair
• Supporting bone and connective tissue health
• Enhancing exercise recovery
• Improving sleep quality

REYORA RESEARCH
BUT WAIT...
NOT EVERY ITCH IS HISTAMINE.
Research shows itch can also be driven by non-histaminergic pathways and other inflammatory mediators.
ITCHING ≠ AUTOMATICALLY A "HISTAMINE REACTION."
HISTAMINERGIC ITCH PATHWAY
1 Mast cells release histamine.
2 Histamine binds to H1 receptors on sensory nerves.
3 Signals are sent to the brain, resulting in itch.
KEY MEDIATORS: Histamine, H1 receptors, tryptase, prostaglandins, leukotrienes, others.
VS.
NON-HISTAMINERGIC ITCH PATHWAYS
1 Other mediators (e.g., cytokines, neuropeptides, proteases) are released.
2 These activate different receptors or ion channels.
3 Signals are sent to the brain, resulting in itch.
KEY MEDIATORS: Cytokines (IL-31, IL-33), PAR-2, TSLP, nerve growth factor, substance P, others.
Multiple studies confirm that both histaminergic and non-histaminergic mechanisms can contribute to itch—depending on the trigger, the person, and the context.
SCIENCE FIRST. HEALTH ALWAYS.

MECHANISM AND HORMONAL EFFECTS
Fulvestrant is a selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) used to treat hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Unlike aromatase inhibitors, it does not reduce estrogen production but instead binds to estrogen receptors and promotes their degradation.
This effectively blocks estrogen signaling and prevents estrogen-dependent cell proliferation. Because it removes the receptor itself, its mechanism differs fundamentally from receptor blockers or aromatase inhibitors.
panels.scene: Text panel explaining Fulvestrant's mechanism of action with product image and cartoon man.

panels.subject: other

SUMMARY
Fulvestrant is a potent SERD that suppresses
estrogen signaling by degrading the
estrogen receptor itself rather than
lowering estrogen levels. Clinical evidence
supports its effectiveness in hormone
receptor-positive breast cancer, especially
in combination therapies.
It is a prescription oncology medication with
specific indications and is not intended for
general hormonal modulation.
The average dosages are 250-500mg

Clinical trials have demonstrated that
fulvestrant significantly improves

RESEARCH TAKEAWAY

BEST FRAMING
Thymulin is the thymus gland primary
hormonal signal to the immune system.
It is the only peptide hormone
produced exclusively by the thymus,
and its zinc-dependent activation
makes it a unique bridge between
mineral status and immune function.

WHAT STANDS OUT
The connection between Thymulin
decline, thymic involution, and immune
aging is one of the most well-supported
mechanisms in immunogerontology. Its
anti-nociceptive and neuroendocrine
effects add research dimensions
beyond straightforward immune
modulation.

USE CAUTION
No completed human clinical trials
exist for Thymulin as a therapeutic
intervention. Its very short half-life
creates real delivery challenges.
Synthetic analogs with improved
stability are under development.
Current evidence is preclinical
and observational.

The Peptide Company
panels.scene: Science-themed infographic about Thymulin hormone

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
WHY IT DREW ATTENTION

IMMUNE AGING RESEARCH
Thymulin levels decline sharply with age as the thymus involutes. Research explored whether restoring Thymulin signaling could slow immune aging, support T-cell output in elderly subjects, and reduce susceptibility to infection and disease in aging populations.

PAIN MODULATION ANGLE
Preclinical research identified Thymulin receptors in the hypothalamus and showed anti-nociceptive effects in rodent pain models. This neuroendocrine connection drew interest from researchers studying inflammatory pain, fibromyalgia models, and central sensitization.

AUTOIMMUNE + INFLAMMATORY RESEARCH
By modulating T-cell differentiation and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines, Thymulin has been studied in autoimmune disease models. Research explored its potential to restore immune balance in conditions characterized by dysregulated T-cell activity.

The Peptide Company
panels.scene: Infographic detailing Thymulin's research applications in immune aging, pain modulation, and autoimmune/inflammatory conditions.

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
EVIDENCE + LIMITS

EVIDENCE LEVEL
Thymulin has a solid preclinical evidence base. Animal studies have demonstrated T-cell maturation effects, anti-inflammatory activity, pain modulation, and immune restoration in aging models.
Some early human studies explored Thymulin levels as a biomarker of immune aging and zinc status.

REPORTED RESEARCH FINDINGS
Preclinical studies showed Thymulin restored T-cell output in aged and zinc-deficient animals, reduced inflammatory cytokines in pain and autoimmune models, and demonstrated anti-nociceptive effects in rodent pain paradigms. Its decline with age correlates with measurable immune deterioration.

CRITICAL LIMITS
No completed human clinical trials exist for Thymulin as a therapeutic intervention. Most data is preclinical or observational.
Thymulin has a very short half-life in circulation, creating significant delivery challenges. Synthetic analogs are being developed to address stability and bioavailability limitations.

The Peptide Company

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
WHAT IS THYMULIN?
THE ZINC-DEPENDENT THYMIC PEPTIDE
Immune Regulation | T-Cell Maturation | Anti-Inflammatory Research

WHAT IT IS
Thymulin is a naturally occurring nonapeptide produced exclusively by thymic epithelial cells. It is the only peptide hormone known to be secreted solely by the thymus, and it requires zinc binding to become biologically active.

ZINC DEPENDENCY
Thymulin exists in two forms: an inactive free form and an active zinc-bound form. The zinc ion is essential for receptor binding and biological activity. Zinc deficiency directly reduces circulating active Thymulin levels, linking immune function to zinc status.

RESEARCH SCOPE
Thymulin has been studied for T-cell maturation and differentiation, immune system aging and thymic involution, anti-inflammatory signaling, pain modulation, and potential applications in autoimmune and immunodeficiency research.
panels.scene: Infographic about thymulin peptide and zinc dependency

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
CORE MECHANISM

PRIMARY SIGNAL
Zinc binding activates Thymulin,
enabling it to bind specific receptors
on T-lymphocyte precursors. This
triggers intracellular signaling
cascades that drive T-cell
maturation, differentiation into CD4
and CD8 subsets, and expression of
T-cell surface markers.

DOWNSTREAM EFFECTS
Active Thymulin promotes T-helper
and T-cytotoxic cell differentiation,
enhances NK cell activity,
modulates cytokine production, and
suppresses pro-inflammatory
signaling. It also influences
neuroendocrine pathways, with
receptors identified in the
hypothalamus.

WHY IT MATTERS
Thymulin is the primary hormonal
signal through which the thymus
communicates with the immune
system. As thymic function
declines with age, Thymulin levels
fall, and with them the capacity to
generate new mature T-cells, a
central feature of immune aging.

Functional Category: Immune modulation / Host defense regulation
Mechanism of Action
Thymosin Alpha-1 (Ta1) is a synthetic version of a naturally occurring thymic peptide involved in immune system regulation. It plays a critical role in T-cell maturation and differentiation, supporting adaptive immune responses.
Mechanistically, Ta1 enhances immune function by modulating toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling and promoting dendritic cell activation. It supports the differentiation and proliferation of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes while improving antigen presentation. Additionally, Ta1 has been shown to modulate cytokine production, balancing pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory responses.
Unlike broad immunostimulants, Thymosin Alpha-1 acts as an immune regulator—helping restore immune competence in states of suppression while preventing excessive inflammatory overactivation.
Clinical and Research Applications
• Chronic viral infection management (e.g., hepatitis B and C in certain regions)
• Immunocompromised state research
• Cancer immunotherapy adjunct studies
• Sepsis and systemic infection investigation
• Vaccine response enhancement research
It has regulatory approval in several countries for specific immune-related indications.
Administration Route

Three Ways A Vial Can Fail

PROBLEM 1 — WRONG DOSE
Many products contain less than half their labeled amount.

PROBLEM 2 — WRONG MOLECULE
Roughly 1 in 3 samples had an incorrect amino acid sequence.
A peptide with one swapped amino acid is a different compound entirely.

PROBLEM 3 — CONTAMINATION
• Bacterial endotoxin — can trigger systemic inflammation
• Heavy metals: lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium
• Residual synthesis solvents from manufacturing

@SOMARESEARCH

Why Gray-Market Means No Guardrails
Pharmaceutical manufacturing follows cGMP — current
Good Manufacturing Practice.
cGMP	Gray Market
Verified purity testing	No purity requirement
Sterility requirements	No sterility standard
Potency guaranteed	Label claims unverified
Regulatory oversight	Zero FDA oversight

No cGMP requirement means no obligation to prove
what's actually in the vial.

@SOMARESEARCH

panels.subject: other
panels.ocrText:
Why Dosing Precision Makes This Worse
Peptides are active at very small amounts — the margin for error is narrow.
A vial labeled at one amount but containing half delivers unpredictable biology.
→ Under-dosed: no meaningful effect, wasted research
→ Unknown sequence: binds different receptors, unknown outcomes
→ Endotoxin present: injected contamination, not a peptide
Precision only matters if the compound is what the label says it is.

WHAT DOES
"RESEARCH USE ONLY"
ACTUALLY MEAN?
When a peptide is labelled "Research Use Only", it
means the product is supplied solely for controlled
scientific and laboratory research.
It is not licensed as a medicine, food supplement or cosmetic
product, and it has not been approved for diagnosing, treating,
or preventing any medical condition.

A RESEARCH MATERIAL
A research peptide is supplied as a laboratory material for scientific investigation.
Researchers may use peptides to study their structure, properties and interactions
within controlled experimental models.

WHAT CAN RESEARCHERS STUDY?
Depending on the peptide, laboratory research may investigate areas including:
• Molecular structure and characteristics
• Receptor interactions
• Cellular signalling pathways
• Peptide stability and degradation
• Protein and peptide interactions
• Biochemical mechanisms
• Behaviour under different
laboratory conditions

WHY DOES "RESEARCH USE ONLY" MATTER?
The label describes the product's intended purpose and distinguishes a research
material from a licensed medicine or other approved consumer product.
A research peptide has not been authorised as a medicine simply because
scientific studies exist about that peptide or related molecules.
Research findings and regulatory approval are two very different things.

RESEARCH ≠ MEDICAL APPROVAL
A substance can be investigated extensively in laboratories and scientific literature
without being an approved treatment.
Scientific research is designed to build knowledge – researchers investigate
mechanisms, test hypotheses and build evidence.

SO WHEN YOU SEE "RESEARCH USE ONLY"...
It means the product is being supplied for legitimate laboratory and scientific
research purposes, rather than as a medicine or treatment.
Understanding that distinction is one of the most important basics when learning
about the world of research peptides.

Peptides are research compounds that work through specific physiological mechanisms. Every mechanism has conditions under which it performs better or worse. A GLP-1 compound that works well for someone eating adequate protein and moving regularly will show a different result for someone who isn't.

panels.ocrText:

Research indicates GHK-Cu can help
neutralize free radicals in cell culture

GHK-Cu is a tripeptide (3 amino acids)
with copper binding, which contributes

GHK-Cu is commonly used in studies related to
skin biology, wound healing, hair biology, neurobiology,
and age-related cellular research.
